entries.title: Advancement Table
entries.summary: The experience point cost table for Arts and Abilities, showing the points needed to buy a score from zero and the points needed to raise it by one. Used in character creation and all later advancement.
quotes: The number of experience points required to raise a score from zero to that number.
To Raise: The number of experience points required to raise a score by one point to that number.

entries.title: Using Experience Points
entries.summary: Explains how experience points raise Arts and Abilities and gives the cost formulas for gaining a level in each.
quotes: INCREASE AN ABILITY BY ONE: (Ability + 1) x 5 experience points
INCREASE AN ART BY ONE: Art + 1 experience points

entries.title: Advancement Tables
entries.summary: Lookup table of the experience points needed to buy a score from zero, or to raise it by one, for Arts and Abilities.
quotes: To buy: The number of experience points required to raise a score from zero to that number.

entries.title: Advancement Total
entries.summary: Defines the Advancement Total earned by a season of study and the rule that only one source of experience may be used per season, apart from Exposure.
quotes: ADVANCEMENT TOTAL: Source Quality + Bonus from Virtues - Penalty from Flaws

entries.title: Calculating Experience Points
entries.summary: Three-step procedure from Source Quality to Advancement Total to experience points gained, and which Virtues and Flaws modify each step.

entries.title: Exposure
entries.summary: The weakest source of experience: simply using or assisting with an Ability or Art during a season; experience may be split between two subjects, and lab work grants Exposure to lead magus and assistants.
quotes: EXPOSURE SOURCE QUALITY: Two

entries.title: Adventure Experience
entries.summary: Adventures give a whole season of experience with a Source Quality set by the storyguide, which can be split among Abilities used and Arts used on stage.
quotes: ADVENTURE SOURCE QUALITY: 5–10

entries.title: Practice
entries.summary: Full-time self-directed study of an Ability, with special higher Source Qualities for native-tongue languages, Area Lore, feedback-rich crafts and practising spells for mastery; Arts cannot be raised this way.
quotes: PRACTICE SOURCE QUALITY: 4–8, usually 4

entries.title: Training
entries.summary: One-on-one instruction by a master who has a higher score and is using the Ability to earn a living; Hermetic Arts cannot be raised by training.
quotes: TRAINING SOURCE QUALITY: Master's score in Ability being taught + 3
TRAINING GAIN LIMIT: Master's score in Ability being taught

entries.title: Teaching
entries.summary: Lessons from a teacher with a higher score and a shared language, with Source Quality depending on the teacher's Communication and Teaching and a bonus that depends on class size; Arts may only be taught one-on-one.
quotes: TEACHING SOURCE QUALITY: Teacher's Communication + Teaching + 3 + bonus
TEACHING GAIN LIMIT: The teacher's score in the Art or Ability

entries.title: Arcane Studies
entries.summary: Points out that Art scores and Magic Theory can be raised in several ways, all described in the Experience and Advancement section.
quotes: Magi may increase their Art scores in several different ways.

entries.title: Assigning Seasons
entries.summary: Explains how seasons are abstractly assigned to work and study for ordinary characters, and how magi differ because lab work takes a whole real season and they have genuinely free seasons.

entries.title: Gain Limit
entries.summary: A study source with its own level caps the score a student can reach from it, and gives no experience towards the next level.
quotes: This limit is called the Gain Limit.

entries.title: Vis Study
entries.summary: Magi study an Art from raw vis, consuming pawns of that Art's vis for the season; a double botch on the stress die can lead to Wizard's Twilight.
quotes: VIS SOURCE QUALITY: Stress Die + Aura Bonus

entries.title: Grog Yearly Experience
entries.summary: Explains how many experience points a non-magus character gains each year and how those are split between exposure, practice and a vocational season, with adjustments for Poor and Wealthy characters.
quotes: Non-magus characters receive 15 experience points every year.

entries.title: Updating Grogs
entries.summary: A bookkeeping shortcut for advancing grogs: update regular grogs once a year in winter, share the work between players, and handle story experience and infrequently used grogs with training packages.
quotes: all grogs gain 7 experience points in that Ability
The player then applies 4, 2, and 2 experience points to up to three different Abilities

entries.title: Distractions
entries.summary: Distractions of more than a month reduce an Advancement or writing total by a fraction for each full month lost, rounding fractions up.
quotes: For every full month lost, reduce the total by one third of its original amount.

entries.title: Academic Learning and Experience Points
entries.summary: Allows experience from being taught an Academic Ability to be split between that Ability and Latin or Teaching, with a minimum share going to the Ability taught, and similar rules for Latin and Artes Liberales.
quotes: He must put at least half of the gained experience points in the Academic Ability taught
If a player puts experience points gained from Latin instruction into Artes Liberales, he must put at least half of them in Latin.

entries.title: Teachers (Gifted Students and Mundane Teachers)
entries.summary: Mundane teachers dislike Gifted students; The Gift's social penalty applies to Teaching Source Quality for a Gifted teacher and to a Gifted student, and the Parma Magica removes it.
quotes: A character with the Gentle Gift is not penalized, and a character with the Blatant Gift suffers a –6 penalty.

related.text: ArM5 p.75 The Gift social penalty

entries.title: Book Learning for Young Characters
entries.summary: A young student can study summae and tractatus if he can read and has enough fluency in the book's language, subject to the owner's or covenant's limits on access.
quotes: must be fluent in the language used in the book (a score of 4 or higher in the written language)

entries.title: Training an Apprentice
entries.summary: A magus may train an apprentice in Abilities, not Arts, without needing Teaching, though the Training Source Quality is usually lower; it still counts as a season of one-on-one instruction.
quotes: Only Abilities can be trained, not Arts, but a trainer does not need an additional Ability (Teaching) to train, like a teacher does.

entries.title: Studying From Books
entries.summary: Rules for studying summae and tractatus: language and literacy prerequisites, level limits for summae, one-time study of each tractatus, and Supernatural Abilities needing a score of at least one.
quotes: SUMMAE: Source Quality and Level
SUMMA GAIN LIMIT: Summa Level
TRACTATUS: Source Quality

entries.title: Writing Books
entries.summary: Prerequisite scores for writing a useful book and the Source Quality formulas for summae and tractatus.
quotes: SUMMA SOURCE QUALITY: Author's Communication + 6 + bonus
Tractatus Source Quality: Author's Communication + 6

entries.title: Writing Summae
entries.summary: How a summa's Level and Quality are chosen, the Quality bonus for a lower Level, and how many points per season accumulate until the book is finished, with a worked example.
quotes: the summa is complete.

entries.title: Writing Tractatus
entries.summary: A tractatus takes one season to write and has a limit on how many one author can write in a given Art or Ability.
quotes: It takes one season to write a tractatus.

entries.title: Copying Books
entries.summary: Careful copying keeps the original's quality; quick copying is three times as fast but lowers quality; the copyist's Profession: Scribe score drives the pace for summae.
quotes: COPYING CAREFULLY: 1 tractatus per season, or 6 + Profession (Scribe) points towards a summa.
COPYING QUICKLY: Three times as fast as careful copying, copy Source Quality is 1 lower than copied book.

entries.title: Corrupted Copies
entries.summary: Lists the minimum language, Realm Lore and Magic Theory scores a scribe needs to copy a text without corrupting it, since a corrupted text is useless.
quotes: A corrupted text is useless.

entries.title: Hermetic Books: Definition of Categories of Value
entries.summary: Sidebar giving typical Quality ranges for summae and tractatus (excellent, sound, vain, discarded and legendary books) as a function of Level.
quotes: These Summae have a Quality of (25 – Level) or below.

entries.title: Translations
entries.summary: Sets the language and Artes Liberales requirements to translate texts, the time needed for a tractatus or summa, and the Quality penalties for language and cultural differences.
quotes: It takes a season to translate a tractatus.
Translated texts have their Quality reduced by 2, one for language differences and one for cultural differences.

entries.title: Lecture Commentaries
entries.summary: A teaching character can have a scribe record his lectures into a tractatus whose Quality derives from the teacher's Communication and the scribe's skill, optionally improved by editing. Commentaries do not count against the character's normal tractatus limit.
quotes: Lecture Commentary Quality: Teacher's Communication + scribe's Profession: Scribe/2
Edited Lecture Commentary Quality: Original Quality + 1 + bonuses from Virtues
A character can produce a number of lecture commentaries equal to his relevant Academic Ability score.

entries.title: Library Consultation
entries.summary: Optional extended fact-finding research rules: a character spends a season consulting books on a single question, gaining temporary experience, then rolls against the question's Ease Factor. Suited to very hard questions.
quotes: a magus can consult a number of books on the relevant ability up to his Intelligence + Artes Liberales per season
At the end of the season, the magus rolls Intelligence plus the temporarily boosted Ability against the Ease Factor of the question.

entries.title: Studying from the Library
entries.summary: How a magus studies from a large library: while the Art score is below the library's Level the library gives its Quality with a bonus, afterwards it gives only Quality for a limited number of seasons, and several magi studying one subject split the books; includes a worked example.
quotes: A maga whose score in an Art is less than the library's Level in that Art gains the library's (Quality + 3) in experience points in the relevant Art.

entries.title: Aging
entries.summary: Yearly aging roll against the Living Conditions and Longevity Ritual modifiers, the Aging table (apparent age, Aging Points, Decrepitude), and the Crisis procedure, table, medical attention and Creo Corpus remedies.
quotes: AGING TOTAL: Stress die (no botch) + age/10 (round up)
CRISIS TOTAL: Simple die + age/10 (round up) + Decrepitude Score
Characters begin aging in the Winter after they turn 35.

entries.title: Living Condition Modifiers for Disease and Trade
entries.summary: Additional modifiers to the Living Condition modifier on the Aging Roll for lepers, those in a leper colony and those working in bad-air trades or mines, with a worked example.
quotes: A Living Condition modifier is applied to the Aging Roll (ArM5, page 170).

entries.title: A Random Method of Death
entries.summary: An optional method for secretly rolling the age at which non-player characters die, so that lines of inheritance take unexpected turns, with adjustments for wartime. The text warns it is harsher than the standard aging rules.
quotes: Assume that any child has a 25% chance of dying of natural causes before adulthood is reached.
assume a death age of 6 simple dice + 20 years

entries.title: A Random Method of Life
entries.summary: Companion method for a character waiting to inherit: check each person ahead of them for a new legitimate child, then check each child for a random age of death.
quotes: Then roll a die for each, assuming that on average half of them do have a child.

entries.title: A Note on Life Expectancy
entries.summary: Advises storyguides who want female nobles to hold power to cull male NPCs using the random method of death given earlier.
quotes: Players in sagas designed for female nobles to play a significant role need to consciously cull male non-player characters.

entries.title: Improving Living Conditions with Magic
entries.summary: Indirect magical improvement of living conditions for aging rolls, by long-term enchantments on the environment, at the cost of Warping for whatever is under the enchantments.
quotes: For every 40 levels of spells or enchantments used to improve the target living conditions, residents gain a +1 living conditions modifier.
targets under two level 20 enchantments gain two Warping Points each year
Targets under a single level 40 enchantment gain five Warping Points per year

entries.title: Longevity Rituals for Mundanes
entries.summary: Applies the Longevity Ritual rules to people without supernatural abilities, giving the requirements and costs, and lists the drawbacks of Warping, overstaying one's welcome and loss of fertility.
quotes: the magus needs a Creo Corpus Lab Total of at least 30
the beneficiary of the Longevity Ritual gains one Warping Point per year

entries.title: Labor and Livelihood (Labor Points)
entries.summary: Characters who work for a living earn Labor Points each season spent tending their business, multiplied by wealth, and must spend a set number to maintain their enterprise.
quotes: A character gains (primary Characteristic + Craft) or (Communication + Profession) Labor Points per season worked.
It costs 36 Labor Points to maintain a character's business interests at their current level.

entries.title: Improving Wealth and Social Status
entries.summary: Gives the Labor Point costs of moving between Poor, average and Wealthy, what happens when a character loses wealth or status, and the extra season and stories needed to reach higher income bands.
quotes: To move from Poor to average costs 120 points.
To move from average to Wealthy costs 360 points.
Moving to a higher income band costs the Labor Points noted above, but also costs a season of time.

entries.title: Overwork (Reputation Penalties)
entries.summary: Working extra seasons or living below one's means to gain Labor Points faster earns a negative Reputation for impiety or miserliness.
quotes: A character who is not Poor, but works three or more seasons in a year, gains a negative Reputation.
This imposes 1 or 3 experience in a Reputation for miserliness every year.

entries.title: Labor Points from Stories
entries.summary: Stories that improve a character's economic or social status award extra Labor Points, scaled by how central the merchant is to the story.
quotes: Half a season's worth of Labor Points when they are a subplot of a more significant story, dealt with by magi.
Two seasons' worth of Labor Points when the merchant is the central character of the story.

entries.title: Investing Time
entries.summary: Characters can invest Labor Points as time or profits to improve their business, treated as minor stories that are not actually played.
quotes: Characters may invest their time or profits, as represented by Labor Points, to improve their businesses.

entries.title: Covenant Craftsmen
entries.summary: Options for deciding how covenant craftsmen relate to guilds, from simply treating all of them as regular craftsmen to making them expelled, runaway or illegal guild members, and how trade-based covenants sell their goods.
quotes: The simplest method is to make every craftsman a regular craftsman.

entries.title: Crafting Items (Seasonal Production)
entries.summary: Introduces the seasonal rules for a craftsman's output, in which craftsmen work only part of the year, and says storyguide craftsmen only need these rules when asked to make a specific item.
quotes: For purposes of the total amount of goods produced in a year, storyguide characters are only allowed three seasons of actual work.
Storyguide character craftsmen are assumed to be busily working in their workshops

entries.title: Working with Related Material
entries.summary: Penalties to a craftsman's Craft score when he works with raw materials outside his usual field, and the loss of his specialization bonus.
quotes: Treat his Craft score as one less for determining his success.
the character's Craft score is penalized by three

entries.title: The Workshop
entries.summary: How long a workshop takes to build, what it costs for inexpensive, standard and expensive goods, and why workshop size does not affect production the way a laboratory's size does.
quotes: Workshops for inexpensive goods cost one Mythic Pound to construct, while those for standard goods cost two, and those for expensive goods cost five.
It takes a season to build such a workshop

entries.title: Workshop Innovation
entries.summary: A workshop has an Innovation score added to its Workshop Total, raised by spending Labor Points and a season of work, with a table of the cumulative Labor Point cost for each level.
quotes: The workshop's Innovation score is added to the Workshop Total.
It takes 100 Labor Points to increase Innovation to +1, 200 more Labor Points for a +2 Innovation score, and another 300 Labor Points to have a +3 Innovation score

entries.title: Raw Materials (Workshop Raw Materials Score)
entries.summary: A workshop has a Raw Materials score improved by spending Labor Points and a season; unlike Innovation it is lost if the responsible character leaves and must be maintained at a Labor Point cost each year.
quotes: It takes 50 Labor Points to increase the Raw Material score to 1, 100 more Labor Points to increase it to 2, and an additional 150 Labor Points to increase the score to 3
It costs 5 Labor Points per point of Raw Material to sustain a business with a positive Raw Material score.

entries.title: Craftsman Workshop Total and Craft Level
entries.summary: Introduces the five quality grades of finished goods and the Workshop Total (primary Characteristic + Craft Ability + the workshop's Innovation and Raw Materials) that a craftsman compares against a Craft Level to see what a season's work produces.
quotes: Workshop Total: Primary Characteristic + Ability + Innovation + Raw Materials
If the Workshop Total equals or exceeds the Craft Level, the character produces a specific amount and quality of finished goods.

entries.title: Primary Characteristic of a Craft
entries.summary: Sidebar saying which Characteristic a craft or labour uses in its formulas (usually Dexterity for craftsmen, Strength for laborers, with exceptions the troupe decides).
quotes: A common rule of thumb is that craftsmen use Dexterity and laborers use Strength.

entries.title: Finished Goods and Quality Craft Levels
entries.summary: Sets the standard Craft Level for a season's work and the Craft Levels needed for shoddy, standard, superior, excellent and wondrous goods; a Workshop Total below standard yields shoddy goods and the storyguide may raise the Craft Level for adverse conditions.
quotes: The standard Craft Level, which assumes adequate space, necessary materials, and no distractions, is 6.
Craft Level for Standard Items: 6
Craft Level for Wondrous Items: 12 + Magnitude of Effect

entries.title: Modifying the Craft Level (situation table)
entries.summary: Sidebar table of situational increases to the Craft Level (war, famine, plague, scarce materials, interruptions, staff changes, non-mundane auras); changing the base Craft Level shifts the levels for every quality grade equally.
quotes: Modifying the basic Craft Level also changes the Craft Levels of different quality goods.
if the storyguide decides that the Basic Craft Level is 9, then a craftsman character needs a 15 to make superior goods and an 18 to make excellent goods.

entries.title: Seasonal Production Chart (scaling output by Craft score)
entries.summary: Explains how to scale the number of items a craftsman makes in a season from his Craft Ability score, and how to convert seasonal output into days per item.
quotes: Divide the character's Craft Ability score by five, then multiply this number by the number of items that a basic craftsman would make in a season.
divide 72 (which is the number of working days in a season, derived from 12 six-day weeks) by the number of items constructed in a season.

entries.title: Standard Quality Items Constructed in a Season (table)
entries.summary: Table of how many standard-quality goods of each kind a craftsman of average skill makes in a season, with the responsible guild and cost band, plus notes on large items that take several seasons and on teams and labor gangs.
quotes: Instead, round to the nearest nice fraction.

entries.title: Shoddy Quality Items
entries.summary: Shoddy goods look and perform like standard goods but break on a botch, and a craftsman can spot them with a Perception roll.
quotes: making a Perception + Craft Ability + simple roll against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: Superior Quality Items
entries.summary: Superior goods give a small bonus to one feature (strength, durability or appearance) for a specific activity; only one such bonus applies to any single roll or total, and the entry gives examples for clothing, tools, shields, swords and armor.
quotes: Only one bonus from a superior or excellent quality item applies to a single total or roll, no matter how many such items are used.

entries.title: Excellent Quality Items
entries.summary: Excellent goods earn extra bonuses for each block of points the Workshop Total exceeds the Craft Level, limited by the creator's Craft Ability, and the bonus applies to every use of the item.
quotes: For every 3 points that exceed the Craft Level, add an additional +1 bonus to a feature of the item.
Total Bonus Limit: Craft Ability / 3, rounded up

entries.title: Workshop Assistants
entries.summary: Craftsmen may employ apprentices or journeymen up to a limit set by Leadership, and each assistant boosts the Workshop Total by a fraction of his own Craft Ability.
quotes: Each assistant adds half his Craft Ability score to the Workshop Total.

entries.title: Craftsman Manuals
entries.summary: A literate craftsman can spend a Labor Point and a season to write a manual of his process; other craftsmen doing that activity may add its score to their Workshop Total, with only one manual usable per season.
quotes: he produces a manual that has a score of one-third his Craft Ability score, rounded up
A craft manual adds its score to the Workshop Total.

entries.title: Workshop Exertion
entries.summary: A craftsman may push his workshop to boost the Workshop Total with a simple die, at the cost of an Aging roll each season and a roll on the Workshop Exertion Results table.
quotes: When a character exerts himself in the workshop, add a simple die roll to the Workshop Total.
For every season that a character exerts himself, the player must make an Aging roll, regardless of the craftsman's actual age.

entries.title: Workshop Exertion Results (table)
entries.summary: Sidebar table and descriptions for the stress-die outcome of exerting in the workshop, from disaster through story events, inventions, increased Reputation and increased understanding.
quotes: Put a simple die's worth of Labor Points towards the workshop's Innovation score.
Add a simple die worth of experience points to the craftsman's (Craft) Reputation score.

entries.title: Craftsman Reputations
entries.summary: Each craftsman has a (Craft) Reputation that rises with excellent seasons and wondrous items and falls with repeated shoddy work.
quotes: Any season a craftsman has a Workshop Total 6 or more points over the necessary Craft Level to produce standard quality goods, the character earns 1 experience point.

entries.title: Selling Finished Goods
entries.summary: A craftsman may roll to haggle a better price, either against a fixed Ease Factor or in opposition to an important customer, with the price moving in fixed percentage steps up to a maximum.
quotes: Presence + Bargain + simple die vs. Ease Factor 9
If successful, the character sells the item for 10% above its standard cost.

entries.title: Basic Laborer's Service
entries.summary: Laborers use a Labor Total compared against a Profession Level in the same way craftsmen use Workshop Totals, producing shoddy, standard or superior service but never excellent or wondrous.
quotes: Labor Level is the laboring character's primary Characteristic + Profession Ability and the Profession Level has a base of 6

entries.title: Damaged Goods: Stress Checks and Damage Levels
entries.summary: When a story event or a botch threatens a valued item, its owner makes a stress check; failures remove damage levels, which depend on the item's quality and Size, until the item breaks. Covers modifiers, botches, unnatural use, and the different fate of wondrous and Hermetic items.
quotes: Stress Check: stress die + modifiers vs. Ease Factor 15
If the stress check fails, the item loses one of its damage levels.
Wondrous items made by craftsmen cease to function if they sustain any damage.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults (House Verditius repairs)

entries.title: Locks and Keys (making, breaking, picking)
entries.summary: Sidebar on crafting locks (a high base Craft Level boosted by Artes Liberales), their doubled damage levels, and the rolls for breaking, pulling apart or picking a lock at different qualities.
quotes: Locks are very hard to make, and the base Craft Level is 15, which is subject to the same modifications as other Craft Levels.
Make a Dexterity + Legerdemain + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 12 to open a standard quality lock.

entries.title: Repairing Damaged Goods
entries.summary: A craftsman who could make an item can repair it without a roll over a season, paying Labor Points per damage level, but broken items cannot be repaired.
quotes: He must also spend one Labor Point for every damage level he repairs.

entries.title: The Workshop (Craftsman Grog)
entries.summary: Describes a grog craftsman's workshop through Innovation and Raw Materials, improved by spending excess Labor Points; Innovation passes to the next generation while Raw Materials carries a yearly upkeep cost.
quotes: Each workshop is described through two characteristics, Innovation and Raw Materials

entries.title: Craftswomen and Default Workshop Statistics
entries.summary: Discusses women crafters in the Order's setting and gives a shortcut set of workshop statistics for standard, journeyman and master workshops so grog Labor Points need not be tracked.
quotes: Innovation 1, Raw Materials 2
Innovation 2, Raw Materials 2

entries.title: Craftsman Assistants
entries.summary: Limits the number of assistants a craftsman may employ and explains how their Craft scores contribute to the craftsman's Workshop Total.
quotes: Each assistant adds half his Craft Ability score to the Craftsman's Workshop Total.

entries.title: Labor Points (sidebar)
entries.summary: Defines Labor Points as a measure of a worker's day-to-day output in seasons spent earning Exposure, how many are needed per year to keep a business or crop going, and how a foreman can pool workers' points.
quotes: An individual must accumulate 36 Labor Points in a year to maintain his business or grow his crops.
he accumulates a number of Labor Points equal to three times his Communication + Profession Ability, or his Dexterity + Craft Ability

entries.title: Trained Groups of Animals
entries.summary: A handler may lead tamed animals in combat as a trained group, using Animal Handling in place of Leadership, with exceptions to the usual Combat Score matching.
quotes: The character's Animal Handling Ability score is used instead of his Leadership Ability score

entries.title: Animal Training and Commanding Beasts
entries.summary: A trainer spends seasons building training points against an animal's Might, and once the animal is trained the trainer rolls to have it obey commands of varying difficulty. The same rules serve riders training mounts, who may use Ride in place of Animal Handling.
quotes: This total is the character's Intelligence + Animal Handling – Creature's Might.
a mundane animal is considered to have a Might score of 1 + 2 x Confidence Score
Presence + Animal Handling + stress die vs. a variable Ease Factor

entries.title: Training Animals (Training Points)
entries.summary: Seasonal procedure for taming a mundane animal: a trainer accumulates training points each season until they equal the animal's Might, with a penalty for The Gift; also notes how Might is derived for mundane animals and that training is individual-specific.
quotes: Intelligence + Animal Handling + Animal Ken – Creature's Might – Gift Penalty
Mundane Animal Might = 1 + (2 x Confidence Score)

entries.title: Taming Creatures
entries.summary: A seasonal activity in which a character accumulates taming points from Intelligence + Animal Handling until a threshold based on the creature's Confidence is exceeded, plus rules for commanding tamed animals, building or transferring their Loyalty, and training their Abilities.
quotes: The taming is complete when the accumulated total of points exceeds a total equal to 1 + (2 x the creature's Confidence Score).
Each additional season of training increases the Loyal Personality Trait by +1, to a maximum of +3.
make a Loyalty test for the animal against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: Training Creatures
entries.summary: Any magical beast with Cunning may be tamed over seasons by a magus, magical character or mundane trainer, then trained in tricks.

entries.title: Taming Animals
entries.summary: Taming is a seasonal activity accumulating points over consecutive seasons until they exceed the creature's Might.
quotes: Taming is complete when the accumulated total of points exceeds the Might of the creature.
Required Points to Tame a Creature: Might of the Creature

entries.title: Taming Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Gives mundane beasts an effective Might for taming purposes and notes that Gift penalties apply because taming is social.
quotes: mundane beasts have an effective (Animal) Might of 1 + 2 times Confidence Score

entries.title: Mundane Trainer
entries.summary: A mundane trainer accumulates taming points from Intelligence and Animal Handling less the creature's Might, so can only tame weakly magical beasts.
quotes: Taming Points Accumulated Each Season by a Mundane Trainer: Int + Animal Handling – Creature's Might

entries.title: Tricks, Stunts, and Tasks
entries.summary: A tamed animal can be commanded by characters with Intelligence and Animal Handling or to whom it is loyal, and is not under a continuing mystical effect.

entries.title: Animal Loyalty
entries.summary: A tamed creature gains a Loyal Personality Trait toward its tamer, which can be raised or transferred with extra seasons and tested with a Loyalty Test.
quotes: Loyalty Test: Loyal Personality Trait + stress die vs Ease Factor
Each additional season of training increases the Loyal trait by +1, to a maximum of +3.

entries.title: Training Animal Abilities
entries.summary: Characters with Animal Handling can train a tamed animal's Abilities with the standard training rules, with a Loyalty test for new Abilities.
quotes: make a Loyalty test for the animal against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: Trained Groups of Animals
entries.summary: A character can lead tamed animals in combat as a trained group, using Animal Handling instead of Leadership to set group size.

entries.title: Commanding a Creature
entries.summary: Commanding a tamed creature is a Presence plus Animal Handling roll against an Ease Factor set by how familiar, stressful or frightening the task is.
quotes: Command Beast: Presence + Animal Handling (or Ride or Magic Lore) + stress die vs Ease Factor

entries.title: Indulgences
entries.summary: Explains what an indulgence is (a reduction of a priest-decreed penance, not a payment for absolution), how its price scales with the buyer's means and the length of remission, and what a character must do afterwards to gain Reputation experience and a temporary Faith Point.
quotes: The poor donate what they feel they can afford, in most cases six Mythic pennies per season, and the wealthy at least a pound per season.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.58 Faith Points

entries.title: Worship
entries.summary: A free-season activity of fasting, prayer and meditation whose Source Quality comes from the Divine aura of the church, with experience restricted to Church Lore, Concentration, Music and Divine-aligned Abilities or Arts the character already has.
quotes: Worship has a Source Quality equal to the Divine Aura in the church.

entries.title: Good Works
entries.summary: A season spent on charitable deeds, which for clergy may be a non-free season, giving experience in an appropriate Ability and a Faith Point.
quotes: Good works has a Source Quality of 2 in an appropriate Ability, and the character also gains 1 Faith Point.

entries.title: Ordination
entries.summary: Ordination is a seasonal activity ending in an oral examination: the Examination Total is compared with an Ease Factor set by the grade sought, with Reputation consequences for a very good or marginal result, a Faith Point on success, and appeal or petition when the exam is failed or botched.
quotes: Ordination Examination Total: Intelligence + (Church Lore or Civil and Canon Law) + stress die
If the character's Ordination Exam Total is more than double the required Ease Factor
misses the required Ease Factor by less than 6

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Rapid Ordinations
entries.summary: A character ordained through several grades at once, for example when elected bishop, still gains only a single Faith Point from ordination.

entries.title: Vernacular Literature: Writing and Studying Poetry
entries.summary: Vernacular literature has an Aesthetic Quality rather than a Source Quality, and a poet may write it in any language he knows well enough and whose alphabet he can write. Poets can study other poets' work to raise Craft: Poetry, and non-poets can spend a season reading it for exposure experience in Abilities the storyguide picks.
quotes: The poet can write it in any language in which he has a score of 5
The character gains exposure experience points that can apply to any of the various topics the piece might cover.

entries.title: Styles of Music
entries.summary: Each musician character has a base regional style of music, and studying a different style for a season grants a one-time bonus of experience points that grows with the distance of the new style from the character's own.
quotes: he receives a one-time study bonus of 1 to 3 extra experience points

entries.title: Time Spent Creating Artwork
entries.summary: Gives base creation times for different kinds of artwork (a season, a year or decades), scales that time by the piece's Aesthetic Quality, and explains how assistants limited by Leadership and deliberately hurried work change the time taken. Artists also use the usual free and work seasons, with work seasons earning exposure experience.
quotes: multiply it by 1/10 the Aesthetic Quality of the expected finished piece to determine the full length of time required
The creating character can have assistants equal to his Leadership score.
Doing this divides a piece's Aesthetic Quality by half.

related.text: ArM5 p.163 free and work seasons

entries.title: Studying Artwork as an Advancement Source
entries.summary: Artists can study another artist's piece in the same Craft or Profession as a season of study, using half its Aesthetic Quality as the Advancement total. Performances must be practised and contemplated, each work can be studied only once, and a character cannot study his own work.
quotes: Divide the artwork's Aesthetic Quality by two to determine the Advancement total.
Source Quality: Aesthetic Quality/2

entries.title: Aging, the Easy Way
entries.summary: A shortcut for aging old or many characters by looking up the Aging Points gained per decade for mild, average or harsh aging at the character's Aging Score, with a simple-die method to find Apparent Age.
quotes: age/10 (round up) – Living Conditions modifier – Longevity Ritual modifier

entries.title: Aging Chart
entries.summary: Table of expected Aging Points and crises per decade by Aging Score for mild, average and harsh aging, excluding points from crises.
quotes: The Aging Points listed exclude those deriving from crises.

entries.title: Applying Crises
entries.summary: Optional use of the crises listed on the Aging Chart: the character gains a Decrepitude score equal to the crises and additional Aging Points that shrink by fraction with each extra crisis, rounded up.
quotes: if he suffers one crisis, then he gets half of the Aging Points listed in the Aging Chart

entries.title: Effects of Aging on Characteristics
entries.summary: Gives the approximate distribution of Aging Points among Characteristics so they can be applied in line with the Aging Table.
quotes: The Aging Table (ArM5, page 170) is designed to affect certain Characteristics in favor of others.

entries.title: Finding an Apprentice
entries.summary: A magus can spend a season searching for an apprentice with a Perception roll against an Ease Factor, helped by assistants whose own checks lower that Ease Factor.
quotes: The player makes a Perception + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 12 to successfully find an apprentice
The assistant character makes a Characteristic + Ability check against an Ease Factor of 12.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.17 Bonisagus apprentice rules
Houses of Hermes: Societates p.128 Pralix

entries.title: Becoming an Apprentice
entries.summary: How a found child becomes an apprentice, which Abilities a pre-apprentice child may have, and how an untrained child can help in the laboratory by adding to Safety, Aesthetics and a Mentem Specialty.
quotes: The character adds his Intelligence divided by 2 to a lab's Safety, +1 to Aesthetics, and +1 to a Mentem Specialty

entries.title: Teaching Schedule
entries.summary: Sidebar explaining the traditional apprenticeship schedule from Bonisagus' letters: score 5 in all Arts before Opening, one teaching season each year, early Latin and Magic Theory study, and a Gauntlet at the end.
quotes: According to the Peripheral Code, a magus must teach his apprentice for one season every year.
Generally, apprentice magi gain scores of Latin 4, Artes Liberales 1 and Magic Theory 3 by the time they reach adolescence.

entries.title: The Mechanics of a Pilgrimage Story
entries.summary: Defines minor and major pilgrimages and a Pilgrimage Target Level for each desired outcome (gaining or losing Virtues and Flaws, removing traits, penance, miracles), plus limits on which Virtues and Flaws a pilgrimage can change.
quotes: A minor pilgrimage is one that requires a Target Level of 18 and that occurs in a single season, requiring a story.
A major pilgrimage is one that requires a Target Level of 30 and that takes multiple seasons, and possibly multiple stories, to play out.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.60 Miracles

entries.title: Oppositional Elements
entries.summary: How the storyguide builds a pilgrimage story from Oppositional Elements with assigned values that each pilgrim must personally overcome, with a table of example elements by value.
quotes: Total of Oppositional Elements Values = Pilgrimage Target Level
The Oppositional Elements for the pilgrimage should have total value at least equal to the Target Level of the Pilgrimage.

entries.title: An Example of a Pilgrimage Story
entries.summary: A worked example of setting Target Levels, totalling Oppositional Elements and tracking which characters overcome them on a major pilgrimage.

entries.title: Growing Up: Training by Parents
entries.summary: Mundane children learn by copying the same-sex parent; grog and companion parents can spend a free season training a child using their Training Source Quality, and covenant upbringing differs from village life.
quotes: A parent spends one of the free seasons training the child, who receives experience points based on the parent's Training Source Quality.

entries.title: Life in the Covenant (Adolescent Characters)
entries.summary: Adolescent characters follow the same two-work, two-free season pattern as their parents, and can take part in adventures, often being chosen for low-risk missions.
quotes: an adolescent character must work two seasons a year

entries.title: Horses and Aging
entries.summary: Optional aging rules for important horses: lifespan, when a horse begins to age, rolling every season, and the stable bonus that needs a Profession Marshal score; also a loss of horses in a shoddy stable and the carrying capacity rule of thumb in the following sidebar.
quotes: A horse begins to age at 14 years, and must make an aging roll every season thereafter, rather than every year as humans do.
Every five years a horse's aging modifier increases by one.

entries.title: Opening the Arts
entries.summary: Opening the Arts is a season-long procedure that lets an apprentice cast and legally binds the apprentice to the magus; a parens with a low Art score gives the apprentice a Deficiency, which is a crime.
quotes: A magus should have a score of 5 in all 15 Hermetic Techniques and Forms.

entries.title: Teaching Hermetic Virtues
entries.summary: A Gifted parens trained in Magic Theory can teach an Hermetic Virtue he has in one season by generating a Teaching Source Quality that meets a Target Level, which rises with the student's existing Hermetic Virtues and falls if the teacher includes an Hermetic Flaw.
quotes: TEACHING SOURCE QUALITY: Communication + Teaching + 3 + bonus
THE TARGET LEVEL IS 15 TO LEARN A MINOR HERMETIC VIRTUE
THE TARGET LEVEL IS 21 TO LEARN A MAJOR HERMETIC VIRTUE

entries.title: Investments Suited to All Merchants
entries.summary: Introduces the ways any merchant can invest surplus Labor Points or spare seasons.
quotes: All merchant types may invest their surplus Labor Points, or spend their spare seasons, in the following ways.

entries.title: Charity (investing Labor Points)
entries.summary: Giving surplus labor to charity improves Reputation, gives social contacts, and lets the merchant summon a crowd of the people the charity helps, sized by a formula using Communication, Leadership, Reputation and a Social Status Multiplier.
quotes: a number of people respond equal to the character's (Communication + Leadership) x his Reputation resulting from charity work x a Social Status Multiplier.

entries.title: Commodity Speculation (investing Labor Points)
entries.summary: Storing goods in hope of a price rise returns Labor Points each year on the amount invested, requires storage and guards, and can be lost to story events.
quotes: The return for commodity speculation is 1 Labor Point per year for every 10 invested

entries.title: Drawings (trading Labor Points for fine goods)
entries.summary: Merchants can spend Labor Points on sumptuous hand-sized goods, and an introduction-agent activity returns part of the invested Labor Points in exchange for a Favor.
quotes: Every (1 x Wealth Multiplier) Labor Points spent is worth a single sumptuous item of hand tool size or smaller.

entries.title: Marriage Broker (investing seasons)
entries.summary: Spending seasons of Labor Points to arrange a marriage earns Reputation, temporary Social Contacts and Favors owed by the couple or their parents.
quotes: This costs two seasons' worth of Labor Points, which are lost.

entries.title: Market Changes (booms, crop failure, new products)
entries.summary: Story and investment rules for booms (an Intelligence + Area Lore roll with graded outcomes when investing), crop failures and famine, and new products, with the Labor Point gains each can earn.
quotes: a character can detect a boom coming by making an Intelligence + Area Lore roll
A roll of 18 lets a character prepare for years in advance
A product that spawns its own industries provides four seasons worth of Labor Points

entries.title: Smuggling (setting up and investing time)
entries.summary: Smuggling as a story reward and as an investment of time that yields Labor Points from Intelligence and Intrigue, with the Flaw and Virtue that smugglers acquire.
quotes: Smuggling, as an investment of time, earns (Intelligence + Intrigue) x Wealth Multiplier Labor Points per season.

entries.title: Finding Defixiones
entries.summary: Only defixiones whose magic has not yet been released can be studied, and the storyguide should limit suitable finds per searching season.
quotes: A magus may only study those defixiones whose magic has not yet been released.

entries.title: Ancient Texts
entries.summary: Collections of ancient defixio formulae are not rated like books, cannot teach Defixio Lore, but a formula from the same cult as a defixio gives a bonus to the Insight roll.
quotes: do not have Source or Quality ratings

entries.title: Chthonic Sanctuaries
entries.summary: Magic Lore rolls identify that underground cult temples may hold defixiones and point to a region, while Intellego Vim can detect their auras and vis sources.
quotes: Intelligence + Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 12 reveals
An Intelligence + Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 15 provides the general region of an appropriate sanctuary.

entries.title: Can Magi Really Heal Lepers?
entries.summary: Distinguishes Hermetic leprosy from true leprosy (a Divine curse) and notes that magic can offset the disease's living-conditions penalty by improving a colony's conditions.
quotes: imposes a –2 living conditions modifier

entries.title: Asklepios as patron: sleeping in the Hall of Repose
entries.requires: Sleeping in the Hall of Repose at Epidauros
entries.summary: Sleepers in the Hall of Repose may receive healing visions and bonuses to Wound Recovery rolls and to the Lab Total of a Longevity Ritual crafted for them there.
quotes: Sleepers here also gain +12 to their next Wound Recovery roll and a +6 bonus to the Lab Total if a Longevity Rituals is crafted for them here.

entries.title: Decoding the Clay Tablets and Searching for En-Dor
entries.requires: Possession of the Canaanite clay tablets (Ancient Magic)
entries.summary: Deciphering the tablets is a seasonal activity with a stress roll, after which they function as a Summa in Area Lore: Canaan whose Quality falls with each missing tablet. Searching for En-Dor in the field is a further seasonal roll, harder when done as off-site research.
quotes: Decoding is a seasonal activity requiring a stress roll of Intelligence + Hebrew against an Ease Factor of 18.
A complete sequence of six tablets is Level 10 Quality 15, with each missing tablet subtracting three from Quality.
A season's worth of search requires an Intelligence + Area Lore: Canaan roll against an Ease Factor of 18 for success.

entries.title: Copying Unintelligible Tablets
entries.requires: Possession of the Canaanite clay tablets (Ancient Magic)
entries.summary: Copying a text you cannot read risks errors, so copying either goes at half rate or costs Quality in the final translated text. Quick rubbings are fast but also cost Quality.
quotes: Careful copying is done at half the standard rate, while copying at normal speed means –3 Quality for the final, translated text.

entries.title: Making a Journeyman Contract
entries.summary: A table converting the result of a journeyman's contract-bargaining roll into a modifier on the Labor Points he earns, with modifiers for his history with the master, his Craft score and past guild fines.
quotes: Communication + Bargain + (Age/10, rounded up) + a stress die
+2 Appropriate Craft Ability is 8+

entries.title: Tournaments as Income
entries.requires: Errant knight living off the tournament circuit
entries.summary: Applies the Labor Points system to knights who earn a living by tourneying, with seasons needed per year depending on wealth, plus guidelines for extra Labor Points from stories.
quotes: It costs 36 Labor Points per year for an errant knight to sustain himself.
The knight gains Dexterity + Single/Great Weapon Labor Points per season on the tourney circuit.

entries.title: Pilgrimage & Devotion
entries.summary: Gives the Devotion Points a Devoted character earns for pilgrimage to a saint's shrine and for further relevant sites and relics seen along the way.

entries.title: A Destination for Pilgrimage
entries.summary: Describes how a pilgrimage to the Purgatory works, including Oppositional Elements, the Circuit of Saint Patrick and the procedures and dates that govern admission.
quotes: Those wishing to visit the Purgatory must plan to arrive at the island between June 1 and August 15; they will not be admitted outside these dates.

related.text: The Church pp.16-19 Pilgrimages and Oppositional Elements

entries.title: Magical Trainer
entries.summary: A character with Master of (Form) Creatures tames creatures of that Form using his Might and Animal Handling less the creature's Might.
quotes: Taming Points Accumulated Each Season by a Master of Creatures: Trainer's Might + Trainer's Animal Handling – Creature's Might

entries.title: Animal Ken and Taming
entries.summary: Describes how Animal Ken lets a character reason with animals, add to taming totals and give more complex commands.

entries.title: Care of Souls
entries.summary: A priest spends a season preaching to his congregation on a virtue theme, giving willing parishioners a bonus to matching activities for the next year and the priest experience in Leadership, Area Lore or Church Lore; it can be replaced by the aura-tempering rules.
quotes: Care of souls has a Source Quality of 2 for the priest, in Leadership, Area Lore, or Church Lore.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.38 Tempering an Aura

entries.title: Visitations
entries.requires: Bishop, archdeacon or rural dean making visitations
entries.summary: Describes the yearly visitation of parishes by bishops and their deputies, its cost to the parish, retinue size limits by rank, and the experience a season of visitation earns the visitor and retinue.
quotes: A season spent on visitation is worth 2 exposure experience points in Church Lore, Civil and Canon Law, Area Lore, or Ride for the visitor and his retinue.

entries.title: Worship
entries.requires: Christian character with access to a chapel or church (similar activities for other Divine faiths)
entries.summary: A free-season devotional routine whose Source Quality is the Divine aura of the church, spent on Church Lore, Concentration, Music or Divine-aligned Abilities and Arts.
quotes: Worship has a Source Quality equal to the Divine aura in the church.

entries.title: The Garden as a Source of Study
entries.summary: Treats the garden's plants as realia for study in Herbam, and its Stirpes as realia of Hermetic Viresculture, each with a Source Quality and a limited number of uses.
quotes: a magus generates a Source Quality of 6, and can study from the garden six times in total

entries.title: Greater Malediction of Hereditary Madness (Personality Flaws on Aging)
entries.summary: A hereditary curse that adds a Minor Personality Flaw each time the cursed character's Decrepitude increases, chosen on a table by a die plus Decrepitude. A repeated Flaw becomes Major, with no further effect once already Major.
quotes: The curse means that every time Sir Erwan's Decrepitude Score increases he gains a Minor Personality Flaw, in addition to any other aging effects
To determine the Personality Flaw roll a simple die + Decrepitude Score and compare to the list that follows.

entries.title: Shinnui Shem (Changing a True Name to Delay Aging)
entries.summary: A kabbalist spends a season changing a True Name, severing arcane connections and gaining a bonus to future Aging Rolls that ends at the next Aging Point and does not stack with other supernatural bonuses.
quotes: BONUS TO AGING ROLL: (Simple Die + Intelligence + Gematria + Understanding + Book Quality + Dominion Aura) / 5
A character may only be renamed once by Shinnui Shem
